title: frontline-ask-rollup-and-contextual-notes-sep-2026
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact rollup of frontline signals captured Aug–Sep 2026 (CS conversations, SE calls, post-mortems, inbound support threads). The aim: provide product & engineering with contextualized asks, severity/frequency, rough customer impact, and suggested next-step owners. Not a final roadmap—intended as input to the Oct planning cycle.

Methodology / signal sources:
- Channels: weekly CS syncs, AE weekly summary emails, a sample of 28 support threads (P1/P2), 5 technical onboarding calls recorded, and three customer-run inference benchmarks shared via S3.
- Sampling bias: heavier towards mid-market fintech and two large enterprise health customers. Fewer pure-PLG single-developer signals in this batch.
- Note: many requests are surfaced repeatedly in different language; I grouped by intent rather than verbatim text.

Executive summary (top-lines):
- Recurrent asks cluster into three tiers: 1) Resilience & graceful degradation (fallbacks, predictable throttling), 2) Cost control and observability granularity (per-route token breakdown + sampling), 3) Private deployment ergonomics (bootstrap scripts, HSM/KMS patterns, offline model sync).
- Quick-win candidates: per-route cost view (dashboard slice), expanded documented fallback recipes, and a sample TLS/KMS bootstrap script for on-prem installs.
- Strategic asks that need product investment: dynamic routing policies by policy chains (latency vs cost vs regional availability), model variant management (auto-fallback compatible variants), and per-customer token sampling for quality regression alerts.

Grouped requests with context and representative quotes:
1) Resilience & graceful degradation (frequency: high, severity: high)
- Request: deterministic fallback chain when a preferred variant is behind or OOMs. Customers want policy-level control (e.g., prefer quantized variant if latency > X).
- Example quote: "We need the app to never 5xx for routine load spikes—route to cheaper/quantized models rather than failing." — FinApps (midmarket, payments).
- Current workaround: SEs have implemented client-side retries and naive region pinning; brittle and doubles cost.
- Proposed short-term: publish recommended fallback recipes + add UI checkbox for simple two-step fallback (primary -> fallback).
- Proposed medium-term: enable policy DSL in routing config (engineer: infra-routing).

2) Cost telemetry and observability granularity (frequency: very high, severity: medium-high)
- Request: finer-grained cost per route/model/token and sampled token traces for skew detection. Teams want per-endpoint attribution at 95th percentile latency and per-route cost splits in the Console.
- Example quote: "We can’t optimize batching without understanding per-endpoint cost distribution. The aggregate view hides the hot routes." — AdTech startup (high throughput).
- Current workaround: manual token accounting using logs and S3 exports. Time-consuming.
- Quick win: add per-route token & cost columns to the usage table and a downloadable CSV.
- Longer-term: integrate sampled token traces / top-k prompt families into Optimize with anomaly alerts.

3) Private deployment ergonomics and compliance (frequency: medium, severity: high for enterprise)
- Request: clearer onboarding for VPC/private, example HSM/KMS integration patterns, and an offline model sync flow (air-gapped).
- Example quote: "Our security team needs to see the exact bootstrap steps for KMS and model sync—they won’t accept vague docs." — MedLife (enterprise, healthcare).
- Current workaround: solutions engineering runbooks with custom scripts (time intensive).
- Recommended: publish canonical scripts, a hardened sample KMS integration, and a one-page checklist for audits. Consider a future ‘private-starter’ artifact in the onboarding flow.

4) Predictable performance under autoscale (frequency: medium, severity: medium)
- Request: clearer SLO guidance for throughput vs latency under dedicated pools and burst policies; customers want to know what packed GPUs will do under mixed sequence lengths.
- Quote: "We need predictable tail latency for legal/regulatory SLAs—any surprise is a business risk." — LegalTech (mid-enterprise).
- Ask: expand the Dedicated docs with capacity planning templates and example autoscale policies for mixed workloads.

5) Model/version control and rollout observability (frequency: medium, severity: medium)
- Request: more visibility into model variant diffs and per-rollout quality snapshots (prompt-based evals pre/post rollout).
- Quote: "Rollouts feel black-box—we want a snapshot of failing prompts when a model is promoted." — Retail AI (large).
- Short-term: encourage use of existing evals kit; produce an example eval set per customer for canary deployments.

Signal-by-customer shorthand (high level):
- FinApps (midmarket): resilience > cost; cares about fallbacks, small latency budgets, sees bursts during settlement windows.
- MedLife (enterprise): private-deployments + compliance; wants audited KMS integration and offline sync.
- AdTech startup: cost granularity & per-route optimization; heavy throughput, cares about batching and token attribution.
- LegalTech: tail latency predictability; focused on SLA defensibility.

Priority suggestions (CS recommendation):
- P0 (0–6 weeks): per-route cost column / CSV export (Console), published fallback recipes + 1-page cookbook, sample KMS bootstrap script for private installs. (Owners: product-console, solutions-eng).
- P1 (6–12 weeks): routing policy presets w/ simple UI toggles (latency-first / cost-first), Dedicated capacity planning templates. (Owners: infra-routing, dedicated-product).
- P2 (quarter+): sampled token traces + anomaly alerts in Optimize, model-variant rollout snapshot tooling. (Owners: optimize, applied-ml).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much backend effort required to add per-route cost attribution at the 95th percentile? Need infra estimate.
- Do we have legal constraints on shipping sample token traces (PII risk)? Coordinate with security & privacy.
- For private bootstrap scripts: which KMS vendors & HSM types should be covered first (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault)? Ask SEs for common patterns.

Risks & friction flags from field conversations:
- Customers use different terminology for 'fallback' (variant vs. model vs. route) which causes mismatch in tickets—recommend glossary in Console and CE training.
- A couple of enterprise AEs indicated they might delay renewals if we don’t provide a private onboarding artifact (KMS + offline sync) in reasonable timeframe (8 weeks). Monitor churn risk.

Suggested next steps (actionable):
- 1-pager for product & eng (this doc attached) + 30-min sync with infra-routing and console teams to confirm feasibility & owners (target: by 2026-09-30).
- Solutions Eng to produce canonical KMS bootstrap draft and share with MedLife for quick validation (target: 2026-10-07).
- Product-Console to scope per-route cost export and a minimal UI addition for fallback checkboxes (est. 2 sprints).

Appendix: raw exemplar snippets (anonymized)
- "Our traffic spikes 3x at 02:00 UTC — we need fast fallback options so we don't eat into our reserved GPU budget." — note from FinApps support thread.
- "On-prem install failed during KMS handshake; we had to open a ticket and wait 48 hours for a custom script." — SE debrief.

Notes to self / TODO for follow-up:
- Pull logs for top-10 routes from Aug & Sep and surface top 5 by tokens/latency for Console scoping (assigned: Diego).
- Security check: sample tracing PII risk assessment (assigned: Priya).
- Capture AE commitments regarding potential renewal pushback (Evan to collate).

If you want a condensed slide or a prioritized Jira epic list from this doc, say the word — I can produce the epic mapping + suggested acceptance criteria for the Oct planning meeting.

-- Aisha
